title: PepMLM designs experimentally binding target-conditioned peptide ligands, including peptides used for targeted protein degradation
summary: PepMLM fine-tunes ESM-2 using masked-language modeling conditioned on a target protein sequence to generate de novo linear peptide binders without structural input. In the reported experiments, selected peptides showed sequence-specific binding to targets including NCAM1 and AMHR2; incorporation into ubiquitin-based antibody constructs enabled targeted degradation of disease-relevant proteins, including Huntington’s disease drivers and viral phosphoproteins.
ai_technology: PepMLM, ESM-2 fine-tuned with target-sequence-conditioned masked language modeling

evidence.tested: In the reported experiments, selected peptides showed sequence-specific binding to targets including NCAM1 and AMHR2; incorporation into ubiquitin-based antibody constructs enabled targeted degradation of disease-relevant proteins, including Huntington’s disease drivers and viral phosphoproteins.
evidence.unknown: The reported evidence is preclinical binding/degradation assays, not therapeutic efficacy, pharmacokinetics or safety. The article notes that experimental optimization/stabilization of its selected peptides was not performed and further validation is needed for viral-target applications. Primary publisher full text/abstract checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Given a target protein sequence, PepMLM generates candidate linear binder peptide sequences by reconstructing masked peptide regions. The authors tested selected designs in binding and degradation assays and reported target-specific activity in the stated systems.
